title: ICP Qualifier Input
description: Input for the icp-qualifier Brick, received via edge mapping from company-profile-lookup. All seven fields correspond to edge-mapped source paths. The conditional invariant on profile_found mirrors the upstream Brick's output contract: profile_found: true requires nonempty fact strings; profile_found: false requires all facts to be null.

company_name.description: Fictional display name from the upstream Brick's catalog lookup. Null when profile_found is false. Not a real-company fact.

industry.description: Canonical industry label from the upstream catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

segment.description: Canonical market-segment label from the upstream catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

audience.description: Canonical audience label from the upstream catalog. Null when profile_found is false.

profile_found.description: True iff the upstream Brick resolved the hostname against its catalog. See the if/then/else block below: true requires the four fact fields to be nonempty strings; false requires all four to be null. When false, the qualifier short-circuits to needs_enrichment without interpreting target_icp.

target_icp.description: Target ideal-customer-profile description, propagated unchanged from the graph input through the upstream Brick. The qualifier interprets this against a closed supported-vocabulary (see SUPPORTED_ICP_VOCABULARY.md). Unrecognized connecting words are ignored. If supported descriptors do not span all three dimensions (industry, segment, audience), the Brick returns needs_enrichment.

notes.description: Optional notes propagated unchanged from the graph input. v0.1: not used in scoring; reserved for future deterministic rules.
